title: How to hear this sermon
english: This is a listening version of John Wesley's sermon, Salvation by Faith. He preached it at Saint Mary's, Oxford, on 18 June 1738. Rendered in modern English.

title: Grace, not our works
english: By grace you are saved, through faith. Ephesians 2:8.

All the blessings God has given us are sheer grace. They are his free kindness, and we do not deserve them. We have no claim on the smallest one. It was free grace that formed man from the dust of the ground, breathed into him a living soul (Genesis 2:7), stamped that soul with the image of God, and put all things under his feet (Psalm 8:6). That same free grace still gives us, today, life and breath and everything else. Nothing we are, nothing we have, and nothing we do can earn the least thing from God's hand. All our works, God himself has worked in us. So those works are further signs of free mercy. And whatever righteousness is found in a person, that too is the gift of God.

How, then, can a sinful person make up for even the smallest sin? With his own works? No. However many they are, however religious they look, they are not his. They are God's. And in fact they are themselves unholy and sinful, so that every one of them needs a fresh atonement. A rotten tree grows rotten fruit. The heart is corrupt all the way through. It has come short of the glory of God, short of the glorious righteousness first pressed into the soul, after the image of its Maker. So a person has nothing to plead. No righteousness. No works. His mouth is stopped before God.

If sinful people still find favor with God, that is grace upon grace. If God still chooses to pour fresh blessings on us, and the greatest blessing of all, which is salvation, what can we say except this: thanks be to God for his gift, too large for words. This is how it is. God shows his love for us in that, while we were still sinners, Christ died to save us. By grace, then, you are saved, through faith. Grace is the source. Faith is the condition.
So that we do not fall short of the grace of God, we have to ask three questions, and ask them carefully.
First. What faith is it, through which we are saved?
Second. What is the salvation that comes through faith?
Third. How do we answer the objections?

title: Not the faith of a heathen
english: First. What faith it is, through which we are saved.
It is not, to begin with, merely the faith of a person who has never heard the gospel.

God does require that person to believe that God is, and that God rewards those who earnestly seek him. God is to be sought by honoring him as God, by thanking him for all things, and by a careful practice of justice, mercy, and truth toward other people. A Greek or a Roman, a Scythian or an Indian, had no excuse if he did not believe at least this much: that God is, and what God is like; that there is a future of reward and punishment; and that moral duty binds us. That is only the faith of a person outside the gospel.

title: Not the faith of a devil
english: Second, it is not the faith of a devil, though that faith goes much further. The devil believes there is a wise and powerful God, kind to reward and just to punish. He also believes that Jesus is the Son of God, the Christ, the Savior of the world. We hear him say it in plain words: I know who you are, the Holy One of God. That is Luke 4:34. We cannot doubt that this unhappy spirit believes every word that came from the mouth of the Holy One, and everything else written by those holy men of old. About two of them he was forced to give this testimony: these men are servants of the Most High God, and they show you the way of salvation. So the great enemy of God and of man believes this much, and trembles while he believes it. He believes that God was made known in the flesh. He believes that God will tread every enemy under his feet. He believes that all Scripture was given by the inspiration of God. That is as far as the faith of a devil goes.

title: Not the apostles' earlier faith
english: Third. The faith through which we are saved, in the sense we are about to explain, is not merely the faith the apostles themselves had while Christ was still on earth. They did believe in him. They left everything and followed him. They had power to work miracles, to heal every kind of sickness and every kind of disease. They had authority over demons. And beyond all that, their Master sent them to preach the kingdom of God. Even that is not yet the faith that saves, in the sense of this sermon.

title: Faith in Christ
english: What faith is it, then?

In general, it is faith in Christ. Christ, and God through Christ, are its proper objects. That, by itself, marks it off completely from the faith of the old pagans, and from the faith of people today who do not know him. And it is marked off from the faith of a devil by this. It is not only a thought in the head. It is not a cold, lifeless agreement. It is not a chain of ideas. It is a disposition of the heart. Scripture says: with the heart a person believes, and so is counted righteous (Romans 10:10). And: if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

Here is how it also differs from the faith the apostles had while our Lord was still on earth. This faith admits the necessity and the merit of his death, and the power of his resurrection. It admits his death as the only sufficient way to redeem man from eternal death, and his resurrection as the restoration of us all to life and immortality. He was handed over for our sins, and raised for our justification. Christian faith, then, is not only agreement with the whole gospel of Christ. It is a full reliance on the blood of Christ. It is trust in the merit of his life, his death, and his resurrection. It is a leaning on him as our atonement and our life, given for us, and living in us. And because of that, it is a closing with him, and a cleaving to him, as our wisdom, our righteousness, our sanctification, and our redemption. In one word, as our salvation.

title: A present salvation
english: Second. What salvation it is, that comes through this faith.

Whatever else it includes, it is a present salvation. It is something a person can reach on earth, and something believers do reach, here. The apostle says it to the believers at Ephesus, and in them to the believers of every age. He does not say, you will be saved, though that is also true. He says, you are saved, through faith.

You are saved, to put the whole of it in one word, from sin. This is the salvation that comes through faith. This is the great salvation the angel announced before God brought his firstborn into the world: you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins. Neither here, nor anywhere else in holy Scripture, is that promise cut down. All his people, all who believe in him, he will save from all their sins. From original sin and from actual sin. From past sin and from present sin. From sins of the flesh and sins of the spirit. Through faith in him they are saved both from the guilt of sin and from its power.

title: Saved from guilt and fear
english: First, from the guilt of all past sin. The whole world is guilty before God. If he kept a strict count of what is done wrong, no one could stand. By the law comes the knowledge of sin, but not deliverance from it. By doing the deeds of the law, no person is counted righteous in his sight. But now the righteousness of God, which is through faith in Jesus Christ, is shown to all who believe. They are justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. God put him forward as the sacrifice that covers sin, through faith in his blood, to show his righteousness in the forgiveness of sins that are past. Christ has taken away the curse of the law, by being made a curse for us. He has blotted out the record that stood against us, taken it out of the way, and nailed it to his cross. There is therefore now no condemnation for those who believe in Christ Jesus.

And being saved from guilt, they are saved from fear. Not from the childlike fear of offending a Father. They are saved from slavish fear. From the fear that has torment in it. From the fear of punishment. From the fear of the wrath of God. They no longer look at him as a harsh master. They look at him as a generous Father. They have not received again a spirit of slavery. They have received the Spirit of adoption, by whom they cry out, Abba, Father (Romans 8:15). The Spirit himself bears witness with their spirit that they are children of God. They are also saved from the fear of falling away from the grace of God and missing the great promises, though they are not saved from the possibility of it. So they have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. They rejoice in the hope of the glory of God. And the love of God is poured into their hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to them (Romans 5:5). By this they are persuaded, though not always, and not always with the same fullness, that neither death nor life, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, can separate them from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

title: Saved from the power of sin
english: Again. Through this faith they are saved from the power of sin, and not only from its guilt. The apostle says: you know that he was shown to us to take away our sins, and in him there is no sin. Whoever abides in him does not go on sinning. That is 1 John 3. Again: little children, let no one deceive you. The person who practices sin is of the devil. Whoever believes is born of God. And whoever is born of God does not practice sin, for God's seed remains in him, and he cannot go on sinning, because he is born of God. And again: we know that whoever is born of God does not go on sinning. The one begotten of God keeps himself, and the evil one does not touch him. 1 John 5:18.

The person who is born of God, by faith, does not sin in these ways. He does not sin by a habit of sin, because a habit of sin is sin reigning, and sin cannot reign in anyone who believes. He does not sin by a willful sin, because his will, while he abides in the faith, is set against all sin, and hates it as deadly poison. He does not sin by a sinful desire, because he continually desires the holy and perfect will of God, and by the grace of God he stifles any drift toward an unholy desire at the start. And he does not count his weaknesses as sin, whether in act, word, or thought, because those weaknesses have no agreement from his will, and without that agreement they are not properly sins. So the one who is born of God does not practice sin. He cannot say he has never sinned. But now, he does not go on sinning.

title: Justification and the new birth
english: This, then, is the salvation that comes through faith, even in the present world. A salvation from sin, and from the consequences of sin. Both are often gathered into the word justification. Taken in its largest sense, justification means a deliverance from guilt and punishment, by the atonement of Christ actually applied to the soul of the sinner who now believes in him. And it means a deliverance from the power of sin, through Christ formed in his heart. So the person who is justified, or saved by faith, is indeed born again. He is born of the Spirit into a new life, which is hidden with Christ in God. And like a newborn child he gladly receives the pure milk of the word, and grows by it. He goes on in the strength of the Lord his God, from faith to faith, from grace to grace, until at last he comes to a mature person, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ.

title: Faith does not cancel holiness
english: Third. The objections.
The first usual objection is this. To preach salvation, or justification, by faith alone, is to preach against holiness and good works.
A short answer is enough. It would be, if we spoke, as some do, of a faith cut off from holiness and good works. We do not. We speak of a faith that produces all good works, and all holiness.

It is worth taking the objection more slowly, because it is not a new one. It is as old as Paul's time. Even then people asked, do we cancel the law through faith? We answer, first, that everyone who does not preach faith does cancel the law. They do it openly, by comments and limits that eat the spirit out of the text. Or they do it indirectly, by never pointing to the only means by which the law can actually be kept. Second, we establish the law. We show its full reach, and its spiritual meaning. And we call everyone to the living way by which the righteousness of the law may be fulfilled in them. These people, while they trust in the blood of Christ alone, use every means of grace he has appointed. They do the good works which God prepared beforehand for them to walk in. And they enjoy, and they show, every holy and heavenly temper. The same mind that was in Christ Jesus.

title: Faith does not excuse pride
english: But does preaching this faith lead people into pride?

It may, as an accident. So every believer ought to be warned, in the words of the apostle. Because of unbelief, the natural branches were broken off, and you stand by faith. Do not be proud. Fear. If God did not spare the natural branches, take care that he does not spare you either. Look at the kindness and the severity of God. Severity on those who fell. Kindness toward you, if you continue in his kindness. Otherwise you too will be cut off. And while a person continues in that kindness, he will remember Paul's words, which see this objection coming and answer it. Where, then, is boasting? It is shut out. By what law? By a law of works? No. By the law of faith. If a person were justified by his works, he would have something to boast about. There is no boasting for the one who does not work, but believes in the one who justifies the ungodly. Romans 4:5. The words before and after our text say the same thing. God, who is rich in mercy, even when we were dead in sins, made us alive together with Christ. By grace you are saved. He did it to show the immeasurable riches of his grace, in his kindness toward us in Christ Jesus. For by grace you are saved, through faith, and this is not your own doing. Neither your faith nor your salvation comes from yourselves. It is the gift of God. The free gift. The gift we do not deserve. The faith through which you are saved, and the salvation which God, of his own pleasure and mere favor, joins to that faith. That you believe is one instance of his grace. That, believing, you are saved, is another. Not by works, so that no one may boast. All our works, all our righteousness before we believed, earned nothing from God but condemnation. They were so far from deserving faith, that faith, whenever it is given, is not from works. And salvation is not from the works we do after we believe, either. For then it is God who works in us. And if he gives us a reward for what he himself works, that only commends the riches of his mercy. It leaves us nothing to boast about.

title: Mercy, despair, and comfort
english: But may talk like this, about the mercy of God saving and justifying freely by faith alone, encourage people to sin?

It may, and it will. Many will go on sinning so that grace may abound. Their blood is on their own head. The goodness of God ought to lead them to repentance, and so it will, for the person who is sincere. When they learn that there is still forgiveness with him, they will cry out that he would blot out their sins too, through faith in Jesus. And if they cry earnestly and do not give up, if they seek him in every means he has appointed, if they refuse to be comforted until he comes, he will come, and he will not delay. He can do a great work in a short time. The Acts of the Apostles is full of this faith being worked in people's hearts, like lightning from heaven. In the same hour that Paul and Silas began to preach, the jailer repented, believed, and was baptized. So did 3,000, at Peter's preaching, on the day of Pentecost (Acts 2:41). They all repented and believed at that first preaching. And, blessed be God, there are many living proofs now that he is still mighty to save.
Set the same truth at another angle, and people make the opposite objection. If a person cannot be saved by all that he can do, this will drive people to despair.

True. It will drive them to despair of being saved by their own works, their own merits, or their own righteousness. And so it should. No one can trust the merits of Christ until he has utterly renounced his own. The person who goes about to establish his own righteousness cannot receive the righteousness of God. The righteousness that comes from faith cannot be given to him while he trusts the righteousness that comes from the law.
But this, they say, is an uncomfortable doctrine.

The devil spoke like himself, that is, without truth and without shame, when he dared to suggest that. It is the only comfortable doctrine. It is full of comfort, to every sinner who has destroyed himself and condemned himself. Whoever believes in him will not be put to shame. The same Lord over all is rich toward all who call upon him. Here is comfort, high as heaven, stronger than death. What? Mercy for everyone? For Zacchaeus, a public robber? For Mary Magdalene, a common harlot? I can almost hear someone say: then I, even I, may hope for mercy. And so you may, you afflicted one, whom no one has comforted. God will not throw out your prayer. He may say, in the very next hour: take heart. Your sins are forgiven. Forgiven so fully that they will not reign over you anymore. And the Holy Spirit will bear witness with your spirit that you are a child of God. Glad news. News of great joy, sent to all people. Come, everyone who is thirsty. Come to the waters. Come, and buy, without money and without price. Whatever your sins are, though they are red like crimson, though they are more than the hairs of your head, return to the Lord, and he will have mercy on you. Return to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.

title: Preached first
english: When the objections run out, we are simply told that salvation by faith alone ought not to be preached as the first doctrine. Or, at least, that it ought not to be preached at all.

What does the Holy Spirit say? No one can lay any other foundation than the one that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. So then, whoever believes in him will be saved. That is, and must be, the foundation of all our preaching. Which means it must be preached first.
Well, someone says, but not to everyone.

To whom, then, are we not to preach it? Whom shall we leave out? The poor? No. They have a special right to have the gospel preached to them. The unlearned? No. From the beginning, God has revealed these things to unlearned and simple people. The young? Not at all. Let the children come to Christ, and do not forbid them. Sinners? Least of all. He did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.

If anyone is left out, it would have to be the rich, the learned, the respectable, the moral people. And it is true that they often leave themselves out of the hearing. Even so, we must speak the words of our Lord. The commission runs like this: go, and preach the gospel to every creature. If anyone twists it, or any part of it, to his own destruction, he must carry his own load. But still, as the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to us, that we will speak.

title: Why it has to be spoken now
english: And we will speak it at this time especially. By grace you are saved, through faith. Never was the defense of this doctrine more timely than it is now.

Nothing else can really stop the spread, among us, of the Romish delusion that a person is put right with God by his own merits and religious works. It is endless to attack, one by one, every error of that church. Salvation by faith strikes at the root, and where this is established, the rest falls at once. This is the doctrine our own church rightly calls the strong rock and foundation of the Christian religion. It is what first drove Popery out of these kingdoms, and it alone can keep it out.

Nothing else can check the immorality that has spread over the land like a flood. Can you empty the ocean, drop by drop? Then you might reform us by warnings against one vice at a time. But let the righteousness which is from God, by faith, be brought in, and those proud waves will be stopped.

Nothing else can stop the mouths of people who glory in their shame, and openly deny the Lord who bought them. They can talk as loftily about the law as the person who has it written by God on his heart. To hear them, you might think they were not far from the kingdom of God. Take them out of the law and into the gospel. Begin with the righteousness of faith. Begin with Christ, the end of the law for everyone who believes. Then the people who a moment ago looked almost Christian, or altogether Christian, stand revealed as sons of perdition. As far from life and salvation, God be merciful to them, as the depth of hell is from the height of heaven.

title: Luther and the doxology
english: For this reason the adversary rages whenever salvation by faith is declared to the world. For this reason he stirred up earth and hell to destroy the people who first preached it. And for the same reason, knowing that faith alone could overturn the foundations of his kingdom, he called out all his forces, and used every art of lies and slander, to frighten Martin Luther from reviving it.

We should not be surprised. As that man of God observes: how it would enrage a proud, strong, armed man, to be stopped and set at nothing by a little child coming against him with a reed in his hand. Especially when he knew that little child would surely overthrow him, and tread him under foot.

Even so, Lord Jesus. Thus has your strength always been made perfect in weakness. Go out, then, you little child who believes in him, and his right hand will teach you terrible things. Though you are helpless and weak as an infant of days, the strong man will not be able to stand before you. You will prevail over him, and subdue him, and overthrow him, and trample him under your feet. You will march on, under the great captain of your salvation, conquering and to conquer, until all your enemies are destroyed, and death is swallowed up in victory.

Now thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. To him, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honor, and power, and might, for ever and ever. Amen.
